extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs); state air agencies; small businesses and their representatives; regulatory and legal stakeholders involved in EPA rule implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the regulatory standards, criteria, and procedural requirements in the EPA final rule preamble and associated amendments for New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and emission guidelines addressing greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER determination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The final NSPS and emission guidelines reflect the application of the BSER that, taking into account costs, energy requirements, and other statutory factors, is adequately demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BSER determination must consider statutory factors including costs and energy requirements; standards should reflect the application of that BSER and be adequately demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must be cost‑effective and compatible with reliable electricity supply
rubrics_metrics.description: These final actions ensure that EGUs reduce their GHG emissions in a manner that is cost-effective and improve the emissions performance of the sources, consistent with the applicable CAA requirements and caselaw. EPA has designed these standards and emission guidelines in a way that is compatible with the nation's overall need for a reliable supply of affordable electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule design must balance emissions reductions with cost-effectiveness and not undermine grid reliability or affordable electricity supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBAR Panel convening criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA agreed that convening a SBAR Panel was warranted because the EPA solicited comment on a number of policy options that, if finalized, could affect the estimate of total compliance costs and therefore the impacts on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposed options could affect compliance-cost estimates and small-entity impacts, convene a SBAR Panel and solicit small entity representative (SER) input; accompany with IRFA and solicited comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity screening analysis method
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate the number of small businesses potentially impacted by the NSPS, the EPA performed a small entity screening analysis for impacts on all affected EGUs by comparing compliance costs to historic revenues at the ultimate parent company level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review historical data and planned builds (since 2017 in this case) to determine universe of additions; use ultimate parent company revenues as denominator; follow SBA size standards to identify small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of compliance costs to small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the costs of the rule were calculated, the costs attributed to small entities were calculated by multiplying the total costs to the share of the historical build attributed to small entities. These costs were then shared to individual entities using the ratio of their build to total small entity additions in the historical dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute aggregate compliance costs proportionally based on historical/planned build share, then allocate to individual entities by their share of small-entity builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic/financial impact metric thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA assessed the economic and financial impacts of the rule using the ratio of compliance costs to the value of revenues from electricity generation, focusing in particular on entities for which this measure is greater than 1 percent (and also noting a 3 percent threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag entities with compliance-costs/revenue ratios ≥1% (or ≥3%) for closer scrutiny; example: of 14 entities considered, three ≥1% in 2035 and none ≥3%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of regulatory alternatives to minimize small-entity impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the SBAR Panel recommendations and comments, EPA is finalizing several regulatory alternatives that could accomplish the stated objectives of the Clean Air Act while minimizing any significant economic impact of the final rule on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit alternatives from SERs/RTOs and commenters; evaluate and, where feasible, adopt alternatives that meet statutory objectives while reducing small-entity burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short‑term reliability emergency mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The short-term reliability emergency mechanism, which is available for both new and existing units, is designed to provide an alternative compliance strategy during acute system emergencies when reliability might be threatened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism intended for acute system emergencies; provides temporary alternative compliance pathway to preserve reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism for units planning to cease operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability assurance mechanism will be available for existing units that intend to cease operating, but, for unforeseen reasons, need to temporarily remain online to support reliability beyond the planned cease operation date. This mechanism requires an adequate showing of reliability need, and whether to grant an extension to an owner/operator is solely the decision of the EPA (FERC concurrence is not a condition but may inform EPA's decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when insufficient time exists to complete a state plan revision; states may incorporate these instruments into plans and they will be presumptively approvable if they meet emission-guideline requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive approvability condition for state plan reliability instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: These instruments will be presumptively approvable, provided they meet the requirements defined in these emission guidelines, if states choose to incorporate them into their plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State incorporation of the defined reliability instruments leads to presumptive approvability so long as emission-guideline requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to evaluate subcategories for small entities (rural co-ops, small utilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA solicited comment on potential exclusions or subcategories for small entities based on class, type, or size of the source and whether rural electric cooperatives and small utility distribution systems (serving 50,000 customers or less) can expect to have access to hydrogen and CCS infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate access to low-GHG fuels/technologies, increased energy costs, transmission upgrade costs, and infrastructure encroachment when considering subcategories; EPA may decide not to establish a separate subcategory if not warranted by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low‑GHG hydrogen BSER pathway decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing the low-GHG hydrogen BSER pathway, having assessed that the cost of low-GHG hydrogen in 2030 will likely be higher than proposed and that its nationwide availability and associated uncertainties weigh against designating it as BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost estimates, availability, and associated uncertainties are key inputs when deciding whether a technology (low-GHG hydrogen) constitutes BSER.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS BSER pathway decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: For CCS, EPA considered geographic availability of sequestration, as well as the timelines, materials, and workforce necessary for installing CCS, and determined they are sufficient. The BSER is premised on source-to-sink CO2 pipelines and sequestration, with noted synergies in rural areas from existing ethanol-industry CO2 infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sequestration geography, pipeline/source-to-sink logistics, deployment timelines, supply chain (materials) and workforce availability, and potential cross-industry synergies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Entity Compliance Guide publication
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is preparing a Small Entity Compliance Guide to help small entities comply with this rule. The guide will be available 60 days after publication of the final rule at the specified EPA webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tailored compliance guidance and resources for small entities within a defined post-publication timeframe (60 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: UMRA applicability and written statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NSPS contain a Federal mandate under UMRA that may result in expenditures of $100 million or more for the private sector in any one year. Accordingly, EPA prepared, under section 202 of UMRA, a written statement of the benefit-cost analysis which is in section XIII.A of this preamble and in the RIA. The repeal of the ACE Rule and emission guidelines do not contain an unfunded mandate of $100 million or more for state, local, and tribal governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule may impose private‑sector expenditures ≥ $100 million in any year, prepare the UMRA section 202 written statement of benefit-cost analysis; estimate burdens for state/local plan development and determine if they exceed $100 million.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism consultation and cooperative federalism approach
rubrics_metrics.description: These actions do not have federalism implications as defined in E.O. 13132. Consistent with the cooperative federalism approach directed by the Clean Air Act, states will establish standards of performance for existing sources under the emission guidelines set out in this final rule. EPA nonetheless consulted with 10 national 'Big 10' organizations and other state/local professional groups to provide background and solicit input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when federalism implications are not triggered, meaningful consultation with state and local elected-official organizations and relevant professional associations is appropriate to secure timely input on rule development and implementation burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation and applicability (E.O. 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: These actions do not have tribal implications as specified in E.O. 13175. The emission guidelines do not directly impose specific requirements on EGU sources located in Indian country, and tribes are not required to develop plans; EPA would consult with leaders from affected tribes before developing any standards for sources on tribal land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer government-to-government consultation and outreach consistent with EPA policy when tribal interests exist; determine applicability to tribal lands before imposing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 13045: evaluate effects on children and vulnerable populations for significant regulatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is subject to E.O. 13045 because it is a significant regulatory action and EPA evaluated the environmental health and welfare effects of climate change on children and other vulnerable populations. EPA concluded CO2 emission reductions will improve air quality and benefit children's health, citing literature on vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For significant regulatory actions with potential disproportionate effects on children or other vulnerable groups, assess and document likely risks and benefits to those populations using literature and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 13211: Statement of Energy Effects and quantified energy impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: These actions are likely to have a significant adverse effect on the supply, distribution or use of energy; EPA prepared a Statement of Energy Effects estimating a 1.4 percent increase in retail electricity prices on average in 2035, a 42 percent reduction in coal-fired electricity generation in 2035, and a 3 percent increase in delivered natural gas prices in 2035. EPA also conducted a Resource Adequacy Analysis documented in the RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rule may significantly affect energy supply/distribution/use, prepare an energy-effects statement, quantify projected price and generation impacts, and analyze resource adequacy to show compliance can be achieved while maintaining reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTTAA / 1 CFR part 51: search for voluntary consensus standards and IBR requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This rulemaking involves technical standards. EPA conducted searches in the NSSN database for applicable voluntary consensus standards (VCS) (no applicable VCS identified for EPA Method 19) and, in accordance with 1 CFR part 51, is incorporating multiple voluntary consensus standards by reference in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for applicable VCS via NSSN/ANSI and either adopt VCS by reference (with IBR approvals and citation to CFR sections) or explain why no VCS applies (e.g., none identified for a method). Provide purchase/contact info for standards bodies to demonstrate availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards incorporation by reference (specific standards and their purposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is incorporating by reference specific ANSI, ASME, ASTM, and ISO standards (e.g., ANSI C12.20-2010 for electricity meter accuracy used to measure hourly electric output; ASME PTC 22 and PTC 46 for performance tests; various ASTM standards to define fuel types; ISO 2314 for combustion turbine acceptance tests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify each standard, its edition/date, the measurement/performance purpose it serves in the rule, and which CFR sections reference it; identify availability and sources for purchasing the standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: §60.17 Incorporation‑by‑reference approvals and CFR cross‑references
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.17 is amended to list IBR approvals for specific standards, showing which sections of the CFR each standard is approved for (e.g., ANSI C12.20-2010 IBR approved for §§ 60.5535(d); 60.5535a(d); 60.5860b(a); ASME PTC 22-2014 IBR approved for §§ 60.5580; 60.5580a; ISO 2314:2009 IBR approved for §§ 60.5580; 60.5580a, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit cross-references in the CFR so regulated parties know which IBR standard applies to which regulatory requirement and where to find the authority citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart TTTT purpose and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart establishes emission standards and compliance schedules for the control of GHG emissions from a steam generating unit or an IGCC facility that commences construction after January 8, 2014, commences reconstruction after June 18, 2014, or commences modification after January 8, 2014, but on or before May 23, 2023. It also establishes standards and schedules for stationary combustion turbines with similar date ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines temporal applicability windows for covered source categories (construction/reconstruction/modification date cutoffs) and identifies source types (steam generating unit, IGCC, stationary combustion turbine) to which subpart standards and compliance schedules apply.
